n: According to its heading, David wrote this after pretending to be insane to escape a Philistine king. Having escaped, he vows to praise the Lord always. Like Psalm 25, it is an alphabet acrostic in Hebrew.

f.w: I will bless the LORD at all times

f.g: To bless God is to praise him with gratitude.

n: David boasts — not in himself, but in the Lord. The humble will hear his story and be encouraged.

f.w: make her boast in the LORD

n: An invitation to praise together: “magnify” means to make God great in our eyes and words.
David testifies simply: I sought the Lord, he answered, and he freed me from every fear.

f.w: delivered me from all my fears

n: Those who look to God are lit up with joy, their faces radiant instead of ashamed.

f.g: Made radiant, glowing — like Moses’ face after being with God.

n: David calls himself “this poor man” — humble and in need. God heard and saved him from all his troubles.
The angel of the Lord sets up camp around those who reverence God, guarding them like a protecting army.

f.w: The angel of the LORD encampeth

n: A beloved invitation: don’t just hear about God’s goodness — experience it for yourself, like tasting food.

f.w: O taste and see that the LORD is good

n: Those who reverence God lack nothing truly needed.
Even strong young lions can go hungry, but those who seek the Lord won’t lack any good thing. Strength is not the same as security.

f.w: they that seek the LORD shall not want any good thing

n: David turns teacher, like a parent gathering children: let me teach you what it means to reverence the Lord.

f.g: Reverent awe and loyal obedience toward God.

n: A teacher’s question: Who wants a long, good life? The next verses give the answer.
First, guard your speech — no evil words, no deception.
Second, turn from evil and do good. Don’t just wait for peace — chase after it.
God is attentive to the righteous; his eyes watch over them and his ears hear their cries.

f.w: his ears are open unto their cry

n: But God sets his face against evildoers, and their memory will fade from the earth.

f.w: cut off the remembrance of them
f.g: Their name and legacy will be forgotten.

n: When the righteous cry out, the Lord hears and rescues them.
God draws close to the broken-hearted and saves the crushed in spirit. A broken heart and contrite spirit is the offering Christ asks of his disciples.

f.g: Crushed, humbled; deeply sorry for sin.

n: Being righteous doesn’t mean having no trials — the righteous have many. But God brings them through all of them.

f.w: Many are the afflictions of the righteous

n: God protects even the bones of the righteous. John saw this fulfilled when the soldiers did not break Jesus’ legs at the cross.

f.w: not one of them is broken

n: Evil itself destroys the wicked, and those who hate the righteous will be held guilty.
The final promise: the Lord ransoms his servants, and none who trust him will be condemned.

f.g: Buys back, rescues — fulfilled in Christ’s Atonement.
